title: Traumatic Pneumothorax
scenario: A 24-year-old male is brought to the emergency department after a motor-vehicle collision in which the steering wheel struck his left chest. He reports sharp left-sided chest pain and increasing shortness of breath.

lines: 24-year-old male arrives by EMS after MVC with steering-wheel impact to the left chest. Reports sharp left-sided pleuritic chest pain, rated 8/10, and progressive dyspnea. Diminished breath sounds over the left lung fields. Bruising noted across the left anterior chest wall. Alert and oriented x3, anxious and restless.
Two large-bore IVs established. High-flow oxygen applied. Trachea midline. Chest x-ray and labs ordered. Client increasingly short of breath and splinting the left side on inspiration.

Provider inserted a left-sided chest tube to a water-seal drainage system per order. Immediate rush of air noted; tidaling present in the water-seal chamber. Occlusive dressing secured at insertion site.
Client reports breathing is much easier, pain now 3/10. Breath sounds improving over the left base. Gentle bubbling in the suction-control chamber; tidaling continues with respiration.
Morphine 2 mg IV every 2 hours PRN for pain
Insert left-sided chest tube, connect to water-seal drainage with suction
Maintain occlusive dressing at insertion site
Keep drainage system below chest level
Continuous pulse oximetry and cardiac monitoring
Notify provider for sudden absence of tidaling or new subcutaneous emphysema

children.subject: Medical-Surgical

options.text: Diminished breath sounds over the left lung

children.rationale: Diminished breath sounds, hypoxia, tachypnea, and pleuritic pain all point to a collapsing lung from pneumothorax and require prompt intervention. Normal orientation and temperature do not.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects impaired oxygenation, impaired ventilation, or both. Each finding may support more than one.
children.rationale: A low PaO2 and SpO2 indicate impaired oxygenation, while a rising PaCO2 and the resulting respiratory acidosis (low pH) indicate impaired ventilation. Marked hypoxia with tachypnea reflects both.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the most urgent risk to monitor for is {2}.

choices.text: impaired gas exchange from lung collapse
acute pain from chest wall bruising

children.rationale: Lung collapse impairs gas exchange, the immediate physiologic threat, and it can progress to a life-threatening tension pneumothorax if air continues to accumulate. Pain, anxiety, and later complications are lower priority.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Place the client in semi-Fowler's position
Clamp the chest tube during transport for a bubbling air leak
Encourage deep breathing and incentive spirometry

children.rationale: Oxygen, upright positioning, chest-tube insertion, and lung expansion exercises all treat a pneumothorax. Clamping a tube with an active air leak can trap air and cause a tension pneumothorax, so it is contraindicated.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: After the chest tube is connected to the water-seal drainage system, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the drainage system below the level of the chest
Monitor the water-seal chamber for tidaling
Ensure the occlusive dressing at the insertion site is intact
Assess bilateral breath sounds and oxygen saturation
Strip and milk the tubing routinely every hour
Clamp the tube whenever the client ambulates

children.rationale: Keeping the system dependent, watching for tidaling, protecting the insertion site, and reassessing breath sounds and oxygenation are core chest-tube care. Routine stripping and clamping during ambulation are unsafe and not indicated.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate that treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Breath sounds improving over the left base
New subcutaneous emphysema at the neck

children.rationale: Improved oxygenation, respiratory rate, breath sounds, and pain show the lung is re-expanding and the pneumothorax is resolving. New subcutaneous emphysema would signal a worsening air leak, not improvement.
